problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=3 \\ 5{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3}=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

activity_context.topic_title: Solving 3x3 Singular Systems of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
examples.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14078399/assets/a39dfc581111c2601dd5851c16fccc086a980a84b7804ef0d0800252016dce83.png)
Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
examples.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 19 \\ 1 & -3 & -8 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 12 \\ 1 & -3 & -8 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 12 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y-6z=7 \\ 0x+y+2z=4 \\ 0x+0y+0z=3\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = 3,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & 16 & -8 & 24\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & 16 & -8 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 16 & -8 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x+2y-z=3
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=3-2y+z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2y+z \\ y=y \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $y,z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3-2y+z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
